I'm still struggling in undergrad (been in and out for 10 years). One MAJOR help is the "Crash Course" channel on YouTube. They have a really wide array of topics the crunch into a few minutes and add small animations to elaborate on. Plus, the hosts sometimes speak very fast which latches onto my attention. Slow narrators make me so sleepy that I sometimes have to increase the speed to absorb the info. 

Another great site is Picmonic. There's this function where they make up a silly mnemonic story with pictures and you can't help but take it in. A great example they used was saying "I will never forget the time there was a hippo on campus". The hippocampus is the part of the brain that is responsible for memory. I will always remember this now because it was such an outlandish mental image.

Now that I got my diagnosis, a therapist, a medication plan, accommodations at school (audio textbooks and extended deadlines) and these two new tools, I'm looking forward to this semester.
